Maximal Fat Oxidation Kinetics (SIN Model)

Source: R/MFO_kinetics.R
MFO_kinetics.Rd

Fit the SIN model (Cheneviere et al., 2009) to describe fat oxidation kinetics and extract three parameters: dilatation (d), symmetry (s), and translation (t). Also calculates Fatmin (the intensity where fat oxidation reaches zero), which is a unique capability of the SIN model over polynomial methods.

Usage

MFO_kinetics(
  MFO_data,
  fatmin_threshold = NULL,
  fit = c("absolute", "normalised"),
  ci = c("none", "parametric", "bootstrap"),
  B = 2000,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

MFO_data

a data frame obtained from the MFO function (must contain FAT and porc_VO2 columns).

fatmin_threshold

`NULL` (default) for Fatmin at the second zero of the curve, or a proportion of MFO in (0, 1), e.g. 0.05, for the intensity above Fatmax where fat oxidation falls to that fraction of MFO (closed form: \[(pi + 2d) ((pi - asin(threshold)) / pi)^(1/s) - d - t\] / K). v0.2.0 used a fixed 5 % threshold searched on a grid.

fit

`"absolute"` (default since 0.3.0-beta.1) or `"normalised"` (see *Normalised or absolute fit*).

ci

`"none"` (default), `"parametric"` (also `TRUE`) or `"bootstrap"` (see *Fit uncertainty*).

B

number of replicates (default 2000).

conf

confidence level (default 0.95).

seed

optional integer for reproducible intervals; the random state of the session is restored afterwards.

Value

Returns a list which contains:

  • MFO_kinetics_data: `MFO_data` plus normalized %MFO (`porc_MFO`, 100 = highest observed FAT, or the fitted MFO with `fit = "absolute"`).

  • MFO_kinetics_plot: ggplot object with the observed %MFO, the basic SIN and the fitted SIN.

  • d: dilatation parameter (width of the curve).

  • t: translation parameter (horizontal shift along intensity axis).

  • s: symmetry parameter (controls curve shape asymmetry; <1 left-skew, >1 right-skew).

  • Fatmin: exercise intensity (% VO₂max) at the second zero of the curve, or at `fatmin_threshold` of MFO if given.

  • FatMax_SIN: exercise intensity (% VO₂max) at peak fat oxidation from SIN model.

  • R_squared: R-squared of the SIN model fit (on the fitted scale: proportion of MFO, or g/min with `fit = "absolute"`).

  • RMSE: Root mean squared error of the SIN model fit (same scale).

  • d_se: standard error of dilatation parameter.

  • s_se: standard error of symmetry parameter.

  • t_se: standard error of translation parameter.

  • convergence: logical, whether the SIN model converged.

  • fit: `"normalised"` or `"absolute"`.

  • MFO_SIN, MFO_SIN_se: MFO of the fitted curve (g/min) and its standard error with `fit = "absolute"`; `NA` otherwise.

  • ci: with `ci` other than `"none"`, a data frame with estimate, lower and upper for each quantity; otherwise `NULL`.

  • bootstrap: with `ci`, a list with `type`, `B`, `kept`, `conf` and the `replicates`; otherwise `NULL`.

Details

The model is equation \[14\] of Cheneviere et al. (2009, Med Sci Sports Exerc 41: 1615-1625, p. 1618, doi:10.1249/MSS.0b013e31819e2f91 ): $$\%MFO = \sin\{[\pi^{1/s} / (\pi + 2d) \cdot (Kx + d + t)]^s\}, \quad K = \pi/100,$$ x in % VO₂max. Up to v0.2.0 the package computed (pi^(1/s)/pi) + 2d, so its `d` (and `t`) are not comparable with published values (SPEC 6.5, 19).

Fitting procedure

As in Cheneviere et al. (2009), the model is fitted by non-linear least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt, [minpack.lm::nlsLM()], start d = 0, s = 1, t = 0) directly to the observed rows of `MFO_data`, with fat oxidation expressed as a proportion of the highest observed value (%MFO / 100). There is no smoothing and no synthetic grid: v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted the SIN to a fine grid predicted by a third-degree polynomial, which inflated n and shrank the standard errors of d, s and t (SPEC 19, finding 7). R-squared and RMSE are computed on the observed proportions. At least 4 rows are needed for 3 parameters: with fewer the function warns and returns `convergence = FALSE`; with 4 or 5 it fits but warns that the fit is unreliable and that at least 6 steps are recommended (SPEC 6.5).

`FatMax_SIN` and `Fatmin` come from closed forms derived from eq. \[14\]: Fatmax = \[(pi + 2d) 2^(-1/s) - d - t\] / K and, by default, Fatmin = second zero of the curve = (pi + d - t) / K, Cheneviere's definition (SPEC 19, finding 3). Fatmin can lie beyond the last observed step (extrapolation).

Which rows are fitted

`MFO_kinetics()` fits every row it receives. Cheneviere et al. (2009) fitted exercise steps only, and averaged only steps with RER <= 1.0:

  • `MFO(..., RER_cutoff = 1)` reproduces their step selection;

  • `MFO(..., include_basal = TRUE)` adds the resting row to `MFO_db`, so it is also fitted here. This departs from Cheneviere's procedure in the SIN as well as in the P3.

The SIN is sensitive to the last steps because the curve must reach zero: in the example data (`author = "Frayn"`) the last step (74.7 % VO₂max, RER 1.03) has negative fat oxidation.

  • `negative_FAT = "truncate"` (default) sets it to 0 and that point anchors the second zero: d = -0.385, s = 0.910, t = 0.355, FatMax_SIN = 36.2, Fatmin = 76.4 % VO₂max.

  • `negative_FAT = "exclude"` or `RER_cutoff = 1` drops it: d = -0.440, s = 0.539, t = 0.023, FatMax_SIN = 33.2, Fatmin = 85.3 % VO₂max.

Report which option was used when publishing SIN parameters.

What to interpret

With real (noisy) data, d, s and t are not to be interpreted one by one: they trade off against each other and d in particular is poorly identified (in simulated tests with a FAT error of 5 % of MFO its typical error was about twice its true value). What the curve determines well are `FatMax_SIN`, `Fatmin` and, with `fit = "absolute"`, `MFO_SIN`; report and compare those. See `vignette("validation")`.

Normalised or absolute fit

With `fit = "normalised"` (Cheneviere et al. 2009; the default up to 0.3.0-alpha.2) fat oxidation is divided by the highest observed step before fitting. Unless a step falls exactly on the true Fatmax, that step is below the true MFO and the shape is distorted even without noise: in noiseless simulated tests with Fatmax between two steps, d was 0.234 instead of 0.18 (SPEC 13.2, issue #13). `fit = "absolute"` (the default since 0.3.0-beta.1) fits fat oxidation in g/min, FAT = M x SIN, with M (the MFO of the curve, returned as `MFO_SIN`) as a fourth parameter, and has no such bias: in noiseless tests it recovered d, s, t, Fatmax, Fatmin and MFO to 1e-6 whether or not a step fell on Fatmax. It needs at least 5 steps. With noise it removes most of the bias but not the spread of d, Fatmax and Fatmin; MFO improves in both. With a FAT error of 5 % of MFO (200 simulated tests, trained shape) the median error of d went from -0.12 (normalised) to -0.02 (absolute) and that of Fatmin from -0.39 to +0.01 % VO₂max, with similar median absolute errors (d 0.40 and 0.37); MFO (highest observed step vs `MFO_SIN`) from +0.010 to +0.002 g/min, median absolute error 0.013 and 0.008. Full table in `vignette("validation")`. It is started from the normalised estimates. Its intervals covered the truth 92-97 % of the time against 74-93 % for the normalised fit (`vignette("validation")`), which is why it is the default since 0.3.0-beta.1 (SPEC 13.2). With 4 steps it cannot be fitted; use `fit = "normalised"` for a 3-parameter fit, with the warning that 4-5 steps give an unreliable fit. In the plot, an observed step above the fitted MFO shows above 100 %.

Fit uncertainty

`ci = "parametric"` (also `TRUE`) or `"bootstrap"` gives percentile intervals for d, s, t, `FatMax_SIN`, `Fatmin` and, with the absolute fit, `MFO_SIN`, as in [MFO()]: replicates are the fitted values plus new errors, refitted from the estimates. `"parametric"` draws sigma^2 ~ Inv-chi^2(n - p, s^2) and then normal errors (Gelman et al. 2013, ch. 14); `"bootstrap"` resamples modified residuals r / sqrt(1 - h), with h the leverage from the gradient J of the fit, diag(J (J'J)^-1 J') (Davison & Hinkley 1997, 7.4). Replicates that do not converge are dropped and counted.

Warnings and messages

Every warning and message of this function is a classed condition: `mfo_warning_<id>` and `mfo_warning` (or `mfo_message_<id>` and `mfo_message`), with the numbers of the text as fields (for example `mfo_warning_negative_fat` has `n`, the number of steps). The text is English; the classes let a program, such as [run_app()], handle a given warning or word it in another language: `withCallingHandlers(expr, mfo_warning_negative_fat = function(w) w$n)`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Read dfs
data(list = c("basal_df", "MFO_df", "VO2max_df"), package = "MFO")

# Convert to data.frame
basal_df <- data.frame(basal_df)
MFO_df <- data.frame(MFO_df)
VO2max_df <- data.frame(VO2max_df)

# Calculate MFO and Fatmax
result_MFO <- MFO(step_time = 20,
                 db_MFO = MFO_df,
                 db_basal = basal_df,
                 db_graded = VO2max_df,
                 cv_var = "RER",
                 author = "Frayn")

# Calculate MFO Kinetics
result_kinetics <- MFO_kinetics(result_MFO$MFO_db)

# Fatmin at 5 % of MFO instead of the second zero
MFO_kinetics(result_MFO$MFO_db, fatmin_threshold = 0.05)$Fatmin
} # }
